title: Apply Theorem 14: Pythagoras
show: right triangle: ladder 7.4 m as hypotenuse, foot 2.1 m from the wall, wall height h

example.question: A ladder $7{\cdot}4$ m long leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is $2{\cdot}1$ m from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach? Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

steps.say: The wall is vertical and the ground is flat, so there is a right angle between them. The ladder is opposite the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse.

rows.aside: Write Pythagoras: hypotenuse$^2$ = sum of the other two sides squared.

steps.say: Let $\hl{1}{h}$ be the height up the wall. Put the numbers in.
Take $2{\cdot}1^2$ from both sides to get $h^2$ on its own.
Square root both sides, then round to one decimal place.

title: Apply Theorem 15: Converse of Pythagoras
show: triangle with sides 20, 99, 101 cm with the right angle marked

example.question: A triangle has sides of length $20$ cm, $99$ cm and $101$ cm. Show that the triangle is right-angled.

steps.say: If there is a right angle, it is opposite the longest side, so that side is the hypotenuse. Here it is $\hl{1}{101}$.

rows.aside: Test: does the sum of the other two squares equal $101^2$?

steps.say: Square the two shorter sides and add them.
Now square the longest side.
The two results are equal. By the converse of Pythagoras (Theorem 15), the angle opposite the longest side is a right angle.

title: Construct and analyse an enlargement
show: triangle ABC and its enlargement PQR from centre O with rays through corresponding points, |OB|=5, |OQ|=12

example.question: The triangle $ABC$ is enlarged with centre $O$ to give the image $PQR$. $|OB| = 5$ cm and $|OQ| = 12$ cm. The area of $ABC$ is $10$ cm$^2$. Find the area of $PQR$.

steps.say: The scale factor is image length over object length. Use the two lengths from $O$: $\hl{1}{k} = \frac{|OQ|}{|OB|}$.
Lengths grow by $k$, so areas grow by $\hl{2}{k^2}$.
Multiply the area of $ABC$ by $\hl{2}{k^2}$.

title: Apply Theorem 9: Parallelogram: opposite sides and opposite angles equal
show: parallelogram ABCD with opposite angles (2x+15)° and (4x-35)° marked

example.question: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. $|\angle DAB| = (2x + 15)^\circ$ and $|\angle BCD| = (4x - 35)^\circ$. Find $|\angle ABC|$.

steps.say: $\angle DAB$ and $\angle BCD$ are opposite angles. By Theorem 9 opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so put the two expressions equal.
Collect the $x$ terms on one side and the numbers on the other.
Put $\hl{1}{x = 25}$ into the expression for $\angle DAB$.
$\angle ABC$ is next to $\angle DAB$. Adjacent angles in a parallelogram add to $180^\circ$, so take $\hl{2}{65}$ from $180$.

title: Apply Theorem 17: A diagonal bisects the area of a parallelogram
show: parallelogram PQRS with diagonal PR dividing it into two triangles, with area 420 m²

example.question: The area of the parallelogram $PQRS$ is $420$ m$^2$. (i) Find the area of the triangle $PQR$. (ii) $T$ is the midpoint of $[QR]$. Find the area of the triangle $PQT$.

steps.say: The diagonal $[PR]$ bisects the area of the parallelogram. So the triangle $PQR$ is half of $420$.
$T$ is the midpoint of $[QR]$, so $[PT]$ cuts triangle $PQR$ into two triangles with equal bases and the same height. Each is half of $210$.

title: Apply Theorem 18: Area of a parallelogram = base × height
show: parallelogram ABCD with base 12 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm marked

example.question: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram. $|AB| = 12$ cm and the perpendicular distance between $[AB]$ and $[DC]$ is $6$ cm. $|BC| = 8$ cm. Find the area of $ABCD$, and the perpendicular distance between $[BC]$ and $[AD]$.

steps.say: Take $[AB]$ as the base. The height is the perpendicular distance to $[DC]$, which is $6$ cm.
Area of a parallelogram is base times perpendicular height.
The area does not change. Now take $[BC]$ as the base, with $|BC| = 8$, and let the new height be $h$.
